                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Running it locally\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Make sure you have the latest version of Wasp installed by running `curl -sSL https://get.wasp-lang.dev/installer.sh | sh` in your terminal.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Run `wasp db migrate-dev`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Since we are using a main.wasp.ts file, we need to run `wasp ts-setup` initially.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is a current crutch we still need to use because the TS config implementation is still not 100% where Wasp team would like it to be.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Run `wasp start`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This will install all dependencies and start the client and server for you :)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. Go to `localhost:3000` in your browser (your NodeJS server will be running on port `3001`)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'6. Install the Wasp extension for VSCode to get the best DX\n'[39m +
                      [32m"7. Check out the docs for more info on wasp's features and step-by-step guides"[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction to Swarm: Building full-stack apps with Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-11-17, last updated: 2025-11-19, [Read more](https://dev.to/genyus/introduction-to-swarm-building-full-stack-apps-with-wasp-1nc5)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"file is still required, but it's much smaller as it purely handles application-level configuration like authentication and the root component.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Feature-specific configuration now lives in\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'feature.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then we need to configure basic username authentication to enable auth settings:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'app.auth({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'methods: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'usernameAndPassword: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Required, but not used in this tutorial\n'[39m +
                      [32m'onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Migrate the database and compile the project so Typescript is aware of the new entities:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev --name init && wasp compile\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"While the app doesn't yet have any proper business logic, all the boilerplate is valid code and you should be able to confirm the application runs by executing:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm run dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You write your app as high-level config in `*.wasp.ts` files, alongside the usual React, Node, and Prisma code. Wasp compiles it into a full-stack app, ready to deploy anywhere.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp stands for **Web App SPecification**: you describe the full-stack behaviour (specification) of your app in `*.wasp.ts` files, at the level of your thoughts (`route`, `auth`, `job`, ...), then implement the details in the underlying stack (React, Node, Prisma, ...).'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp Spec (main.wasp.ts)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-28, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/general/spec)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You define and configure the high level of your app (pages, routes, queries, actions, auth, ...) in a `main.wasp.ts` file in the root of your project.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call this file the **Wasp Spec**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You build your app by:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Importing the building blocks (`app`, `page`, `route`, `query`, ...) from `@wasp.sh/spec`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Importing your own components and functions adding the import attribute `with { type: "ref" }`.\n'[39m +

                      [32m"The `@wasp.sh/spec` package doesn't exist on npm, but it is generated by Wasp per project, so we can customize it to fit the needs of your app.\n"[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Wasp moves from custom DSL to TypeScript spec and rebrands in Launch Week #12\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-21, last updated: 2026-07-21, [Read more](https://reasoncore.dev/post/wasp-moves-from-custom-dsl-to-typescript-spec-and-rebrands-in-launch-week-12)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The release adds server-side prerendering, updated docs and migration guides, and a TypeScript spec API via @wasp.sh/spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- TS Spec uses a canonical main.wasp.ts in the project root with imports from "@wasp.sh/spec" and examples showing wasp: { version: "^0.24.0" }.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'TS Spec replaces the separate DSL file (main.wasp) and the older TS Config style with a TypeScript-native spec file named main.wasp.ts in the project root.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The canonical imports are provided from the @wasp.sh/spec package.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The canonical import line shown in the docs is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The immediate, concrete changes for developers are visible in three places: the canonical file name (main.wasp.ts at the project root), the @wasp.sh/spec API surface (app, page, query, route, job, api, etc.), and migration guides in the docs for moving from the old DSL and earlier config styles.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Examples in the docs reference wasp: { version: "^0.24.0" }.'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Writing a Seed Function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can define as many **seed functions** as you want in an array under the `db.seeds` field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp now lets you write your full-stack logic as a spec in ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-15, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/blog/2026/06/15/wasp-typescript-spec)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You write the Wasp TypeScript Spec (TS Spec) in `*.wasp.ts` files by constructing the `app` spec object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You do so by using the spec constructors from `@wasp.sh/spec`: `page`, `route`, `query`, `job`, `api`, … . That is your "vocabulary" that you use to specify the parts of your web app, and then compose them all together into one big `app` spec object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }; // React\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The only thing Wasp requires from you is that you export an `app` spec object from the `main.wasp.ts` file.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can try Wasp quickly by running `npm i -g @wasp.sh/wasp-cli@latest`, then `wasp new`, and then just follow the instructions, or go to our docs for detailed instructions and a tutorial.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp: The Batteries-Included Full-Stack Framework That Writes Its ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-13, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://reactlibs.dev/articles/wasp/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a Rails-like, batteries-included framework for JavaScript and TypeScript that lets you describe the high-level shape of your app — its routes, pages, auth methods, data operations, and jobs — in one concise spec, and then leans on a real compiler to generate all the glue code between **React**, **Node.js/Express**, and **Prisma**.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead you install the Wasp CLI globally.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The heart of a Wasp project is its spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As of v0.24.0, you author it in TypeScript as `main.wasp.ts` using the `@wasp.sh/spec` package, which brings proper editor support, imports, and type checking.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Your data models live separately in a standard `schema.prisma` file.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's the smallest interesting spec — an app with username-and-password auth:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: "RecipeApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'title: "My Recipes",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'methods: { usernameAndPassword: {} },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - wasp-lang/wasp: The batteries-included full-stack framework for the AI era. Develop JS/TS web apps (React, Node.js, and Prisma) using declarative code that abstracts away complex full-stack features like auth, background jobs, RPC, email sending, end-to-end type safety, single-command deployment, and more.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-01-30, last updated: 2026-06-29, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp (**W** eb **A** pplication **Sp** ecification) is a Rails-like framework for React, Node.js, and Prisma.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Build your app in a day and deploy it with a single CLI command!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// file: main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }; // Your React code.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import { getTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }; // Your Node.js code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Given a simple `main.wasp.ts` specification file that describes the high-level details of your web app, and `.ts(x)`/`.css`/..., source files with your unique logic, Wasp compiler generates the whole source of your web app in the target stack: front-end, back-end and deployment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Run to install Wasp on OSX/Linux/WSL(Win):\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Wasp's Programmable Spec Lets You Build File-Based Routing in 45 Lines\n"[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp, a batteries-included full-stack TypeScript framework, has always resisted this implicit convention.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, it uses an explicit Spec file (`main.wasp.ts`) where you declare routes, auth, queries, and cron jobs in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'That Spec is now programmable—a standard Node.js program that can import npm packages, read the filesystem, or call APIs.\n'[39m +

                  },

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
